rawFindings.title: Valid single-byte ranges are rejected
rawFindings.explanation: HTTP byte ranges are inclusive, so a range whose start equals its end (for example `bytes=0-0`) is valid. The new manual check treats it as unsatisfiable and returns 416.
rawFindings.suggestion: Change this validation to reject only `end < start`, with a separate check for starts beyond the response length.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Serving a 9-byte file with `Range: bytes=0-0` returns 416 with an empty body instead of 206 with the first byte and `Content-Range: bytes 0-0/9`.

rawFindings.title: Open-ended ranges use an end offset past EOF
rawFindings.explanation: When the client sends an open-ended range like `bytes=3-`, this sets the inclusive end byte to `responseData.length`. The last valid byte offset is `responseData.length - 1`, so the response advertises an invalid `Content-Range`.
rawFindings.suggestion: Use `responseData.length - 1` for omitted ends, and clamp explicit end values to `responseData.length - 1`.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Serving a 9-byte file with `Range: bytes=3-` returns `Content-Range: bytes 3-9/9` while the body only contains bytes 3 through 8; it should report `bytes 3-8/9`.

rawFindings.title: Oversized suffix ranges produce negative start offsets
rawFindings.explanation: For suffix ranges larger than the file, this calculation can make `start` negative. HTTP suffix ranges larger than the representation should start at byte 0, not produce a negative `Content-Range`.
rawFindings.suggestion: Clamp the suffix start with `Math.max(0, responseData.length - Number(parts[2]))` and use `responseData.length - 1` as the inclusive end.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Serving a 9-byte file with `Range: bytes=-100` returns a 206 response with `Content-Range: bytes -91-9/9`; it should return the whole file with `Content-Range: bytes 0-8/9`.
